section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey's products all depend on a shared AI foundation: the model layer and agent infrastructure that determine the quality of work our agents deliver.
Legal is one of the hardest domains for AI: documents run to hundreds of pages, matters can span millions of files, and there is zero margin for error on accuracy.
The AI Platform team builds the foundation that every product and agent team at Harvey builds upon.
This team is early and there's a lot to build: model routing, agent architecture, context management, evals.
Your work here sets the ceiling for what Harvey's AI can do.
section_responsibilities:
- Context Engineering & Agent Infrastructure.
Build the platform-level systems for context management, session state, and memory that all of Harvey's agents and products rely on.
- Model Integration & Routing.
Own the infrastructure that lets Harvey onboard new foundation models fast and route to the right one for every task - a capability every product team depends on.
- Evaluation Infrastructure.
Build the shared eval tooling and frameworks that let every team across Harvey measure and improve AI quality systematically.
- Shared Abstractions.
Create the SDKs, platform primitives, and developer tooling that make it dramatically easier for product teams to ship AI-powered features.
- Design and build abstractions and platform-level systems that improve all of Harvey's agentic products.
- Own infrastructure for model integration, routing, and evaluation that helps Harvey choose and deploy the right foundation model for any given context.
- Build evaluation frameworks and tooling that let every team across Harvey iterate on AI quality effectively.
- Partner closely with product engineering teams, PMs, and design to launch cutting-edge AI products.
- Evaluate, prototype, and integrate the latest advancements in AI and agentic systems as they emerge.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 10+ years of experience building backend systems, with at least 1+ year focused on AI/ML engineering and a track record of technical leadership across teams.
- Experience building and shipping multi-model or multi-provider AI systems in production.
- Familiarity with context management, session state, or memory systems in AI or distributed systems.
You've thought about what the model sees and why it matters.
- A track record of building internal platforms, SDKs, or shared infrastructure that other engineering teams actually adopted - and an understanding of why developer experience matters as much as raw capability.
- Strong judgment about abstractions.
Opinionated about good design but pragmatic about shipping incrementally.
- Excitement about agentic AI and the infrastructure challenges of making autonomous systems reliable when the stakes are real.
- A bias toward full ownership: you navigate ambiguity well and don't wait for a roadmap to start solving problems.
- Bonus: experience building evaluation frameworks, working with agent/function-calling architectures, familiarity with legal or other high-stakes professional services domains, or time at early-stage or hyper-growth startups where the underlying technology changes regularly.
COMPENSATION RANGE
$231,000 - $340,000

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey runs on a fleet of Macs and Windows devices, and every one of them is the front door to how each Harvey employee does their work.
We're seeking a Senior Systems Engineer to own client engineering end to end - Jamf, Intune, Autopilot, Okta device trust, and more, and the automation that ties them together.
This is the person who decides how a laptop gets built, secured, patched, recovered, and retired, and who makes those decisions hold up as we scale across offices globally.
The ideal candidate has run a production device management environment at scale and can move between writing the deployment tooling, debugging a broken enrollment, and pushing for improvements to policy, process, and systems along the way.
section_responsibilities:
- Own the endpoint platform.
Jamf Pro for macOS, Intune and Autopilot for Windows, and the mobile fleet alongside them.
You set configuration standards, patching cadence, and compliance baselines in partnership with Security, and you're accountable for the fleet actually meeting them.
- Engineer the device lifecycle.
Zero-touch provisioning through Apple Business Manager and Autopilot, automated onboarding and offboarding, hardware refreshes, DLP, and forensics.
Where the lifecycle still depends on someone remembering to do something, replace that with code.
- Build the automation the fleet runs on.
Most of this role's leverage comes from tooling - Python and scripts against Jamf, Intune, and Okta APIs, event-driven workflows, and self-service that lets employees fix their own problems.
- Partner with Security on endpoint posture.
Work directly with Security on endpoint policies, EDR coverage, device trust and Okta FastPass, disk encryption and key escrow, browser management, and more.
- Be the final escalation for endpoint issues.
IT Operations handles tier 1 and 2 globally; the problems that reach you are the strange ones.
You'll fix them, and then fix the class of problem so the next person doesn't file the ticket.
- Support a global, in-person-heavy company.
Harvey has offices across the US, EMEA, and APAC.
You'll build for time zones you aren't in, and document and train the team well enough that someone in each location can resolve issues independently.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- Minimum 5 years in endpoint, client, or IT systems engineering, including direct ownership of a macOS MDM environment at 1000+ devices.
- Deep hands-on Jamf experience, plus real Windows management experience via Intune, Autopilot, and Entra.
- Strong scripting and automation ability in Python, Bash, or Swift, with a track record of building tooling against vendor APIs rather than clicking through admin consoles.
- Working fluency with an IdP, Okta preferred, covering SSO, MFA, device trust, and how identity and endpoint policy interact.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, especially with non-technical teams.
- Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-growth, and global environment.
section_preferred:
- Experience running endpoint security tooling in a production environment - CrowdStrike or equivalent EDR, managed Chrome Enterprise, DLP.
- Endpoint work inside a compliance program (SOC 2, ISO 27001).

ROLE OVERVIEW
The Business Development team leads Harvey's partnerships with the cloud hyperscalers, frontier AI labs, inference providers, data suppliers, and emerging open source ecosystem.

Our work spans commercial deal structuring, co-selling, co-development, and co-marketing, working cross-functionally with Finance, Research, Product, Sales, Marketing, and other teams across the company.
As a member of the Cloud & AI team, you will help drive strategic partner initiatives and engagement ranging from new model releases and product launch announcements to commercial agreements and co-marketing campaigns, and own the tactical execution that follows: activating commercial marketplaces, unlocking channel GTM opportunities, accelerating field enablement, and supporting day-to-day requests.
It is a unique opportunity that gives you a front row seat to how fast-growing AI companies work together to drive mutual growth.
This is a zero to one builder role on a team that will grow alongside the partner portfolio.
You will be tasked with working across a wide range of programs and initiatives, including standing up new operational processes and ongoing partner reporting.
Much of what this role touches does not have a defined playbook yet.
The ideal candidate is a strong operator who can bring structure to complex partnerships, move comfortably between strategic work and hands-on execution, and build programs that scale as the team grows.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
As Workplace Specialist, you are Harvey's Workplace team in Toronto.
You run the office end to end: the space, the service partners behind it, the experience employees and clients have in it, and the front door.
You are the person everyone in the office turns to, and the one who actually knows.
Your manager sits in another office and time zone.
You take priorities and standards from them and from the global Workplace team, then run the office with real independence.
You escalate the calls that need a manager: contract terms, spend above your authority, and anything with cost, risk, or precedent attached.
Our Toronto office is a serviced suite at iQ Offices, 302 Bay Street.
Much of your building work runs through the iQ team rather than a traditional landlord, and as Toronto grows you will help shape what the next space needs.
This is a fully in-office role, Monday through Friday, 9:00am-5:00pm, with flexibility for early setups, events, and the occasional after-hours matter.
section_responsibilities:
The Office Standard
- Hold the office to the standard the Workplace team sets for appearance, cleanliness, and readiness, and flag what is slipping before it becomes visible
- Walk the office daily and find maintenance needs, safety concerns, and service gaps before anyone reports them
- Be the first person anyone asks about how the space works
Building & Facilities
- Hold the day-to-day relationship with iQ Offices and building management: work orders, approvals, access, and follow-through
- Manage facilities issues (HVAC, plumbing, lighting, doors, appliances, repairs), managing iQ through resolution, and confirm the fix held
- Coordinate deliveries, freight, and loading dock bookings within the building's rules
- Escalate any building matter that carries cost, risk, or precedent to your manager
Vendors & Food and Beverage
- Keep the Toronto vendor book current: contacts, scopes, performance notes, COIs, and renewal dates
- Hold vendors to scope, address service issues directly, and escalate patterns rather than incidents
- Run the pantry, snack, coffee, and catered lunch program; track consumption and cost per head
- Source local Toronto vendors for catering, supplies, and services as the office grows
Front of House & Guests
- Own the front door: greet employees, candidates, and clients, and manage the visitor experience end to end
- Issue and revoke employee badges and keep building access accurate, to the policy set by Workplace and Security
- Receive and route mail, packages, and couriers
- Arrange cover through iQ reception or a backup plan agreed with your manager when you are out
Employee Experience & Events
- Plan and run Toronto onsite events, celebrations, team lunches, and all-hands viewing logistics, end to end
- Deliver client and executive visits: room sets, catering, AV readiness, and the details that make Harvey look sharp
- Host travelling employees and leaders from other offices, so desks, access, and logistics are ready before they land
Onboarding
- Run the Toronto new hire Day 1: desk setup, badges, building access, welcome, office tour, and swag
- Partner with People Ops and IT so every new hire is set up before they arrive
Space, Supplies & Budget
- Keep the seating chart accurate and execute moves, adds, and changes
- Track desk utilization and flag capacity pressure early, with the data behind it
- Own office supply inventory and ordering, including first aid and emergency supplies
- Submit new and recurring POs via our Procurement platform
- Track Toronto Workplace spend against budget (invoices, POs, cost per head), and partner with Finance on payment
Safety & Compliance

- Serve as first responder during a workplace incident and report it through the process your manager owns
- Keep the office aligned with Ontario workplace health and safety requirements (for example, required postings and first aid kits), with support from People Ops
Systems & the Global Team
- Administer Workplace tools day to day (ticketing, seating, visitor management) and keep records accurate
- Own the Toronto Workplace request queue: resolve what you can, route what belongs to IT, People Ops, or Security

- Adopt global Workplace programs and standards locally, and tell the team where Toronto needs something different
- Partner with IT on conference room and AV readiness

- Direct experience managing vendors and holding them to scope, including the difficult conversation when service slips

- Experience with event and hospitality execution: catering, setups, and the details guests notice
- Comfort tracking spend, invoices, and POs, and turning day-to-day data into a clear picture for your manager

- Experience in a serviced or flex office environment, or supporting an office opening or expansion, is a strong plus

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
We're looking for a Lead Product Owner, Finance Systems to own the systems and workflows that power Harvey's finance organization as we scale globally.
This role sits at the center of our finance technology portfolio: NetSuite as the ERP core, Zip for procurement intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex for spend and card programs, and Metronome for usage-based billing.
You'll help shape the roadmap across that portfolio, prioritize competing demands, and drive changes from discovery through deployment, all in an agile and high-growth environment.
You'll partner closely with Accounting, FP&A, Revenue Operations, Procurement, and Tax, as well as teams across Business Technology (where the Finance Systems team lives) and Security, to translate business needs into scalable, well-governed solutions.
This role is as much advisory as it is technical and hands-on: you'll bring thought leadership to the finance org, sit with stakeholders to understand complex and often ambiguous business problems, solution design the tools and automations, and then execute hands-on in the toolstack.
section_responsibilities:
- Act as the product owner for one or more of Harvey's core finance business process areas (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), along with the systems that serve them.
Run discovery with process owners, define target-state process and system design, own the roadmap, and measure success based on value add output and accuracy.
- Lead the hardest problems in your domain, where there's no established pattern to configure against.
That could be international expansion and the entity, currency, tax, and statutory complexity that comes with it, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Develop and maintain a holistic architecture strategy for the finance applications ecosystem: where each system's boundaries sit, how data moves between them, and what Harvey will need short, mid and long term.
Work with the owners of adjacent enterprise systems, including Workday and Salesforce, on the integrations and handoffs finance depends on.
- Find manual work and eliminate it, replacing spreadsheets, manual data entry, and email-based approvals with core configuration, automated workflows and integrations.
Evaluate new functionality within existing and/or new tooling for best fit at Harvey.
- Configure, maintain, and optimize NetSuite and, dependent on business process ownership determined, own the spend and revenue system workflows that feed the ledger: Zip intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex card programs and expenses, Metronome usage ingestion and downstream invoicing logic, and future tooling for advanced revenue recognition.
Understand, advise and execute on data flows, as well as the upstream product and company-wide data sources that revenue reporting depends on.
- Identify, test, and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across the processes you own in a controlled manner, with clear resulting impact of time savings and manual output eliminated.
- Own quality across your applications, ensuring lightweight SDLC to balance accuracy and agility.
Partner with leadership to set best practices and serve as the mentor and escalation point for peers across Finance and Business Technology on the portfolio's hardest design questions.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 7+ years of hands-on experience as a finance systems professional, including 5+ years of direct NetSuite experience with demonstrated complex configuration depth and supporting a global, multi-entity and multi-currency finance organization.
- Product owner or product manager experience in at least one core finance business process area (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), with extensive depth in that domain: discovery with process owners, target-state process design, proposing tradeoffs or workarounds, and owning a roadmap through delivery.
Familiarity with the adjacent areas matters more than equal depth in all three.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills at various levels of the business and technology organizations: adapting how you make a case depending on the audience, building alignment across cross-functional teams, and saying no to a request and explaining why.
A track record of mentoring peers, setting technical standards, or being the expert others escalate to on hard problems.
- Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous, high-stakes process problems without an existing playbook, operating with a high degree of autonomy while knowing when to pull others in on high-impact decisions.
Examples include international expansion and multi-entity or multi-currency complexity, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Deep understanding of leading and emerging trends in SaaS finance applications and architecture, including where automation and AI are truly driving innovation.
- Direct experience implementing best practices around change management, regression and UAT planning, segregation of duties, and regulatory requirements, while increasing efficiencies.

section_responsibilities:

- Partner with the marketing team to develop content that will resonate with lawyers, tailored to the unique needs of their practice areas and client types.
- Act as the "Voice of the Customer," using your legal perspective to help the broader sales team to develop and implement more effective strategies and synthesize customer feedback for the product team through a legal lens.

- Conduct research and analysis on customers and competitors.

- Executive engagement skills and presence, with an ability to establish strong relationships with key decision makers and build credibility at all levels.

- Location: Germany
- Work eligibility: Must have valid German work rights; Harvey does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role

WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey is looking for a driven, strategic, and entrepreneurial Sales Development Manager to build and lead our first SDR team on the ground in Australia and New Zealand.
This is the first dedicated SDR leadership role in the region.
You'll have a rare opportunity to build a foundational go-to-market programme from scratch, shaping how Harvey engages with the most forward-thinking law firms, professional services organisations, and in-house legal teams.
You'll own everything from hiring and onboarding to coaching and performance management.
You'll partner closely with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps to design a scalable, repeatable pipeline generation engine.
You'll also help shape Harvey's regional go-to-market strategy by refining targeting, messaging, and outbound programmes that resonate with the ANZ legal market.
If you're excited by the idea of building teams, developing talent, and driving impact at a fast-growing AI company transforming legal work, we'd love to meet you!
section_responsibilities:
- Build the ANZ foundation.
Hire, onboard, and develop Harvey's first SDR team in Sydney, and set the team's structure, operating cadence, and performance standards.
- Own regional pipeline performance.
Drive the team's contribution to pipeline across inbound and outbound channels, with an initial focus on enterprise law firms and in-house legal teams, in close alignment with ANZ sales targets
- Set goals and own the metrics.
Define team goals and KPIs, track performance weekly, and use the data to decide where the team focuses.
- Partner cross-functionally.
Work closely with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps to improve lead routing, campaign effectiveness, and pipeline conversion.
Build shared goals, a consistent operating rhythm, and feedback loops across teams, such as AE feedback on lead quality.
- Partner with Account Executives.
Shape SDR-to-AE pairings and joint account planning so the team helps AEs break into complex enterprise accounts.
- Stay nimble.
Redeploy the team quickly as priorities change, whether that's event-driven campaigns, outbound sprints, or inbound surges, rather than locking reps into fixed roles.
- Partner with local leadership.
Stay close to the APAC sales team to understand where they see the biggest challenges and opportunities.
Use that insight to set the team's priorities, working within the frameworks and structures provided by HQ.
- Support every segment.
Work with Enterprise, Mid Market, and SMB teams to break into new logos and build pipeline across the market.
- Coach and develop SDRs.
Deliver hands-on coaching through regular 1:1s, call reviews, and deal strategy sessions.
- Design onboarding and enablement.
Partner with GTM Enablement to create programmes that ramp SDRs quickly and build deep product, industry, and prospecting expertise.
- Refine targeting and messaging.
Continuously test and improve outbound strategies, messaging, and account targeting based on ICP fit and performance insights.
- Leverage data and tools.
Use Salesforce, Salesloft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, and ZoomInfo to track performance and optimise workflows.
- Build a strong team culture.
Foster a high-performance culture grounded in ownership, learning, and collaboration.

- A track record of building sales development teams from the ground up, ideally as a founding member of an SDR or BDR function in Australia.
- Direct experience leading SDRs or BDRs in a high-growth, outbound-focused environment.
- Hands-on experience running both inbound and outbound motions.
- Comfort with ambiguity and rapid change.
You're energised, not unsettled, when priorities shift, and you're excited to be the architect of something new.
- Agency and independence.
You're in tune with your local market and act on what the business needs, without waiting for direction from HQ.
- The ability to influence without authority, navigate ambiguity, and advocate for your team across functions
- A coaching-first leadership style.
You invest in people, celebrate wins, and hold high standards with care.
- A data-driven mindset, with the ability to analyse team performance, uncover insights, and iterate quickly.
- Deep familiarity with modern sales development tools, and the ability to recommend and implement tech stack improvements.
- Excellent communication skills and executive presence, both internally and externally.
- A passion for AI, innovation, and the transformation of knowledge work, especially in professional services and legal.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey ships product every week, and every release changes what our customers, our support specialists, and our AI Support agent need to know.
Today that knowledge lives across fragmented surfaces, and the gap between what's shipped and what's documented shows up directly in ticket volume, resolution time, and the quality of answers customers get.
The CX Knowledge Specialist owns the source of truth: the articles, troubleshooting guides, and product knowledge that specialists and our AI Support agent answer from.
You'll consolidate that knowledge into one well-structured foundation built for both people and AI, keep it accurate as the product moves, and use ticket, search, and agent data to decide what to fix next.
You'll work alongside our Enablement Specialists, who turn that knowledge into training and get the team ready for each launch.
This is a hands-on role for a strong writer and systems thinker who wants to build the knowledge layer an AI-first support organization runs on.
section_responsibilities:
- Audit today's fragmented content surfaces: inventory and tag what exists, flag what's duplicate or stale, and migrate it into one knowledge foundation.
- Own the knowledge base: product support articles, troubleshooting guides, how-tos, and product best practices that specialists and the AI Support agent rely on.
- Structure knowledge for both humans and AI.
Apply taxonomy, metadata, and templates consistently, and write articles that retrieve and chunk cleanly for the AI Support agent as well as for specialists.
- Keep knowledge current through every release.
Track what Product ships, and update or create the affected articles before launch so they're ready for the Enablement Specialists' training and for the AI Support agent.
- Close knowledge gaps at the source by owning the feedback loop.
Triage reports of inaccurate, missing, or buried content from downstream teams, then update the source material.
- Mine ticket signals, search logs, and agent escalations to find missing content, stale articles, and areas with high deflection potential, then prioritize fixes.
- Build AI-assisted workflows for drafting, refreshing, and detecting stale content (prompts, automations, review queues) so knowledge scales without adding headcount.
- Run review cycles, ownership assignments, versioning, and archiving so content stays accurate as the product changes weekly.
- Serve as the day-to-day contact for SMEs in Product, Engineering, AI Support, and GTM Enablement to get content reviewed, validated, and adopted.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 5+ years of experience in knowledge management, support operations, technical writing, or content operations.
- Hands-on experience with knowledge base platforms (Zendesk, Notion, or similar), including structuring, migrating, and maintaining content at scale.
- Comfortable using LLMs in your daily workflow, and able to speak concretely to how you've used them to write, maintain, or improve content.
- A systems thinker who likes structure, and a strong writer who can turn complex technical or legal-product details into clear, retrievable content.
- Comfortable operating at Harvey's pace, where the product changes weekly and content needs to keep up without waiting for a perfect process.
- Uses data (ticket trends, search behavior, QA findings) to decide what to write or fix next, rather than working from a static backlog.
- Builds strong working relationships with cross-functional SMEs quickly, and can get content reviewed and adopted without direct authority.

ROLE OVERVIEW
As a Staff Software Engineer on the Security Engineering team, you will join as a founding team member and build the security foundations that let Harvey put increasingly capable AI agents to work.
You'll lead development of a platform for agents to perform security work, while shaping how agents are sandboxed across our product and internal platforms.
One of the central challenges is enabling models with advanced cybersecurity capabilities to discover and validate vulnerabilities automatically, including through authorized penetration testing, while protecting sensitive data and systems.
You'll build the execution environments, orchestration, and controls that make this possible, and help enable the internal use of open-source models with appropriate protections around inference, tool use, and data access.
You'll work closely with the teams building Harvey's product sandbox and internal AI agent platform, shaping architecture and contributing production code to strengthen execution boundaries.
Your impact will come from shipping systems, establishing a shared technical direction, and making security capabilities reusable across teams.
You'll own work from design through rollout and operation, balancing containment with the reliability, performance, and flexibility that useful agents need.
section_responsibilities:
- Set the technical direction for secure agent execution, working across Security, Infrastructure, and Product Engineering to turn emerging capabilities and risks into a concrete roadmap.
- Design, build, and operate a platform for security agents to discover and validate vulnerabilities within authorized targets and execution boundaries, producing reproducible evidence that engineers can act on.
- Build reusable controls for agent tool use, code execution, network and filesystem access, resource consumption, and workload lifecycle.
Integrate with identity and secrets platforms to limit access to the data and credentials each task needs.
- Partner with the owners of Harvey's product sandbox and internal agent platform to make architectural decisions, implement protections, and integrate shared security capabilities into their execution environments.
- Enable internal use of open-source models alongside infrastructure teams, building protections around model serving, agent execution, and sensitive-data handling.
- Develop adversarial tests, evaluations, and telemetry that verify containment and expose failures.
Build mechanisms to scope, observe, interrupt, and safely terminate agent activity.
- Lead delivery and adoption across teams, mentor engineers, and remain hands-on through implementation and production operation, making clear tradeoffs across security, reliability, latency, and cost.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 10+ years developing and running production software, including technical leadership on initiatives spanning multiple engineering teams.
- Strong software engineering skills in languages such as Go, Rust, Python, or C++, with practical experience in Linux systems, networking, and containerized infrastructure.
- Deep expertise in one or more areas of execution security, such as sandboxing, operating-system isolation, container or virtual-machine security, or platforms that execute untrusted code.

- Experience building shared platforms, services, or libraries and helping other teams adopt them through clear interfaces, documentation, and safe migrations.
- Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems, including observability, failure handling, capacity management, and dependable production operation.
- Fluency with AI-assisted engineering and agentic workflows: you use models to accelerate development, validate their output, and reason about the risks introduced when agents use tools, execute code, or access sensitive data.

section_preferred:
- Experience with microVMs, hypervisors, or sandbox runtimes such as Firecracker, gVisor, or Kata Containers, or Linux isolation mechanisms such as namespaces, seccomp, and Landlock.
- Experience building agent runtimes, tool-execution frameworks, or automated security-testing platforms.
- Experience with vulnerability research, penetration testing, or adversarial evaluation of agent systems, including turning findings into reproducible tests and effective controls.
- Experience deploying or securing self-hosted inference and open-source models, including isolation of model-serving workloads and protection of sensitive inputs and outputs.

WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
In this role, you'll build the data and measurement systems that power our post-training, benchmarking, and agent capability efforts.
You'll own synthetic data pipelines, evaluation design, the tasks and grading behind training environments, and the systems that turn feedback from domain experts into training signals and rewards.
These are tasks where correctness often can't be verified automatically, so defining and measuring quality is a core research challenge.
You'll join a small, high-bar team of hands-on engineers and researchers, where each person owns a large part of the work.
We're looking for research engineers who can build reliable data and evaluation systems, question what a metric actually tells us, and work closely with researchers and legal experts to turn model failures into measurable improvements.
section_responsibilities:
- Build synthetic data pipelines that generate, filter, and curate training and evaluation samples for complex legal reasoning and agentic workflows.
- Design evaluations and verifiers that reflect real legal work, calibrate them against expert judgment, and investigate where they fail.
- Build and maintain capability benchmarks like our Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB), along with product-focused evals that track how models perform on real customer workflows.
- Work with legal domain experts to define quality metrics, rubrics, and other grading mechanisms for training and evaluation.
- Own training and evaluation data quality, including provenance, coverage, and safeguards against contamination.
- Close the loop from product usage and customer feedback to new evaluations and training data, so models improve where customers need them most.
- Partner with researchers to investigate model failures, distinguish real gains from misleading metrics, and use findings to guide training and release decisions.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- Experience building data pipelines, ML evaluation systems, or experimentation tooling, with strong Python skills and ownership of production-quality code.
- A rigorous approach to measurement, including statistical reasoning, experimental design, and understanding when a metric can mislead.
- The ability to translate ambiguous goals or expert judgment into structured datasets, rubrics, and measurable criteria.
- Experience with synthetic data, LLM evaluations, automated raters, or preference data is a plus.
Strong data and measurement engineering experience close to ML model development is valuable even without prior LLM work.

Finance Engineers work on Harvey Deals, a new product built off of Harvey's acquisition of Benchmark.

Finance Engineers understand how investors think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live deal pressure.
In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what investment teams actually need.
It's a team built to make Harvey the platform investment teams can trust with their most important work.
This role is the first Finance Engineer dedicated to private credit.
You will build the credit playbook - demo library, workflow templates, use cases - while running live pilots, and lead the credit practice as the team grows.
section_responsibilities:
Forward Deployed Finance Engineers on the private credit team are former credit investors who left the desk to help build the future of how credit gets underwritten.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey designs and builds for a legal industry being reshaped by AI, moving with the urgency and ambition the moment demands, not just adapting to change but architecting it.
As a Design Systems Designer at Harvey, you will define the foundations that make our product coherent, scalable, and trustworthy as it grows in complexity.
The design system is not just a library of components.
It is the shared language between design, engineering, and AI that ensures consistency, quality, and confidence across every interaction.
This is a design role with unusual technical depth.
You lead with design: craft, systems thinking, and a strong point of view on product experience.
But you're equally at home in architecture and implementation.
You understand how tokens are structured, how components are composed, and how systems are built to scale, and you use that fluency to push the system forward rather than hand decisions over the wall.
We're looking for someone who has lived through the evolution of the discipline, someone who understands not just how modern design systems work, but why they're built the way they are, and where the field is heading, especially as AI-native products reshape what a design system needs to be.
This role will report to the Design org, and will be based in SF, NYC, or Toronto.
section_responsibilities:
1.
Build an AI-native design system that sets the bar for design quality for Design, Engineering, and Product through technical direction and collaboration
- Design, prototype, and ship production-ready system components in tight collaboration with frontend and platform engineering, with shared ownership of quality, performance, and maintainability
- Define and evolve the core design system foundations (components, patterns, and tokens) that scale across complex, AI-powered experiences
- Push both the architecture and the implementation of the system: shape component APIs, token structure, theming, and composition patterns alongside engineering, not downstream of it
- Advocate for technical approaches with confidence, especially in new or ambiguous territory where established patterns don't yet exist
- Embed accessibility, responsiveness, and performance into the system by default
- Establish clear contribution, governance, and deprecation models that balance velocity with system integrity
- Raise the bar for system quality across the product through design reviews, critique, and hands-on work
- Build alignment across Design, Engineering, and Product through technical direction and collaboration
- Anticipate future product and platform needs, evolving the system proactively as Harvey scales
2.
Own AI design and implementation workflows for the design team, establishing best practices for prototyping and shipping with AI
- Establish in-code prototyping patterns that make it easier to be innovative and consistent as designers increasingly leverage IDEs to experiment and ship.
- Define AI-assisted design and implementation workflows, establishing best practices for prototyping and shipping with AI
- Document system usage and best practices in a way that is clear, practical, and trusted by product teams
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 5+ years (Senior) / 8+ years (Staff) of product design experience, with significant ownership of design systems in complex product environments
- A design portfolio that demonstrates high design craft in system-level thinking, but a strong point of view on quality, and visual cohesion
- Deep design systems expertise, including an understanding of the history and evolution of the discipline.
You know why the field moved from style guides to tokens to composable architectures, and you have a point of view on what comes next
- Excellent design engineering communication: you articulate system decisions and tradeoffs fluently to designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners
- Ability to clearly articulate system decisions and tradeoffs to designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners
- Strong knowledge of scalable system architecture and component implementation: component API design, design tokens, theming strategies, and how systems hold up across teams and codebases
- Design Engineer experience preferred, but not required in an AI-first world where the boundary between design and engineering is shifting
- High ownership: you treat the system as a product, not a ticket queue
- Strong opinions, loosely held, being comfortable challenging conventions and evolving best practices as the discipline changes
- Comfort operating in ambiguous problem spaces and bringing structure where it doesn't yet exist
WHY DESIGN SYSTEMS MATTER AT HARVEY
Harvey is an AI-native product.
As the system reasons, responds, and adapts in real time, the interface must remain consistent and legible.
A strong design system ensures that complexity does not leak into the experience.
It enables teams to move faster, reduces cognitive load for users, and builds trust in moments where clarity matters most.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey designs and builds for a legal industry being reshaped by AI, moving with the urgency and ambition the moment demands, not just adapting to change but architecting it.
As a Design Systems Designer at Harvey, you will define the foundations that make our product coherent, scalable, and trustworthy as it grows in complexity.
The design system is not just a library of components.
It is the shared language between design, engineering, and AI that ensures consistency, quality, and confidence across every interaction.
This is a design role with unusual technical depth.
You lead with design: craft, systems thinking, and a strong point of view on product experience.
But you're equally at home in architecture and implementation.
You understand how tokens are structured, how components are composed, and how systems are built to scale, and you use that fluency to push the system forward rather than hand decisions over the wall.
We're looking for someone who has lived through the evolution of the discipline, someone who understands not just how modern design systems work, but why they're built the way they are, and where the field is heading, especially as AI-native products reshape what a design system needs to be.
This role will report to the Design org, and will be based in SF, NYC, or Toronto.
section_responsibilities:
1.
Build an AI-native design system that sets the bar for design quality for Design, Engineering, and Product through technical direction and collaboration
- Design, prototype, and ship production-ready system components in tight collaboration with frontend and platform engineering, with shared ownership of quality, performance, and maintainability
- Define and evolve the core design system foundations (components, patterns, and tokens) that scale across complex, AI-powered experiences
- Push both the architecture and the implementation of the system: shape component APIs, token structure, theming, and composition patterns alongside engineering, not downstream of it
- Advocate for technical approaches with confidence, especially in new or ambiguous territory where established patterns don't yet exist
- Embed accessibility, responsiveness, and performance into the system by default
- Establish clear contribution, governance, and deprecation models that balance velocity with system integrity
- Raise the bar for system quality across the product through design reviews, critique, and hands-on work
- Build alignment across Design, Engineering, and Product through technical direction and collaboration
- Anticipate future product and platform needs, evolving the system proactively as Harvey scales
2.
Own AI design and implementation workflows for the design team, establishing best practices for prototyping and shipping with AI
- Establish in-code prototyping patterns that make it easier to be innovative and consistent as designers increasingly leverage IDEs to experiment and ship.
- Define AI-assisted design and implementation workflows, establishing best practices for prototyping and shipping with AI
- Document system usage and best practices in a way that is clear, practical, and trusted by product teams
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 5+ years (Senior) / 8+ years (Staff) of product design experience, with significant ownership of design systems in complex product environments
- A design portfolio that demonstrates high design craft in system-level thinking, but a strong point of view on quality, and visual cohesion
- Deep design systems expertise, including an understanding of the history and evolution of the discipline.
You know why the field moved from style guides to tokens to composable architectures, and you have a point of view on what comes next
- Excellent design engineering communication: you articulate system decisions and tradeoffs fluently to designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners
- Ability to clearly articulate system decisions and tradeoffs to designers, engineers, and cross-functional partners
- Strong knowledge of scalable system architecture and component implementation: component API design, design tokens, theming strategies, and how systems hold up across teams and codebases
- Design Engineer experience preferred, but not required in an AI-first world where the boundary between design and engineering is shifting
- High ownership: you treat the system as a product, not a ticket queue
- Strong opinions, loosely held, being comfortable challenging conventions and evolving best practices as the discipline changes
- Comfort operating in ambiguous problem spaces and bringing structure where it doesn't yet exist
WHY DESIGN SYSTEMS MATTER AT HARVEY
Harvey is an AI-native product.
As the system reasons, responds, and adapts in real time, the interface must remain consistent and legible.
A strong design system ensures that complexity does not leak into the experience.
It enables teams to move faster, reduces cognitive load for users, and builds trust in moments where clarity matters most.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
We're looking for a Lead Product Owner, Finance Systems to own the systems and workflows that power Harvey's finance organization as we scale globally.
This role sits at the center of our finance technology portfolio: NetSuite as the ERP core, Zip for procurement intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex for spend and card programs, and Metronome for usage-based billing.
You'll help shape the roadmap across that portfolio, prioritize competing demands, and drive changes from discovery through deployment, all in an agile and high-growth environment.
You'll partner closely with Accounting, FP&A, Revenue Operations, Procurement, and Tax, as well as teams across Business Technology (where the Finance Systems team lives) and Security, to translate business needs into scalable, well-governed solutions.
This role is as much advisory as it is technical and hands-on: you'll bring thought leadership to the finance org, sit with stakeholders to understand complex and often ambiguous business problems, solution design the tools and automations, and then execute hands-on in the toolstack.
section_responsibilities:
- Act as the product owner for one or more of Harvey's core finance business process areas (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), along with the systems that serve them.
Run discovery with process owners, define target-state process and system design, own the roadmap, and measure success based on value add output and accuracy.
- Lead the hardest problems in your domain, where there's no established pattern to configure against.
That could be international expansion and the entity, currency, tax, and statutory complexity that comes with it, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Develop and maintain a holistic architecture strategy for the finance applications ecosystem: where each system's boundaries sit, how data moves between them, and what Harvey will need short, mid and long term.
Work with the owners of adjacent enterprise systems, including Workday and Salesforce, on the integrations and handoffs finance depends on.
- Find manual work and eliminate it, replacing spreadsheets, manual data entry, and email-based approvals with core configuration, automated workflows and integrations.
Evaluate new functionality within existing and/or new tooling for best fit at Harvey.
- Configure, maintain, and optimize NetSuite and, dependent on business process ownership determined, own the spend and revenue system workflows that feed the ledger: Zip intake and approvals, Ramp and Brex card programs and expenses, Metronome usage ingestion and downstream invoicing logic, and future tooling for advanced revenue recognition.
Understand, advise and execute on data flows, as well as the upstream product and company-wide data sources that revenue reporting depends on.
- Identify, test, and implement practical AI and automation opportunities across the processes you own in a controlled manner, with clear resulting impact of time savings and manual output eliminated.
- Own quality across your applications, ensuring lightweight SDLC to balance accuracy and agility.
Partner with leadership to set best practices and serve as the mentor and escalation point for peers across Finance and Business Technology on the portfolio's hardest design questions.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 7+ years of hands-on experience as a finance systems professional, including 5+ years of direct NetSuite experience with demonstrated complex configuration depth and supporting a global, multi-entity and multi-currency finance organization.
- Product owner or product manager experience in at least one core finance business process area (order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, and/or record-to-report), with extensive depth in that domain: discovery with process owners, target-state process design, proposing tradeoffs or workarounds, and owning a roadmap through delivery.
Familiarity with the adjacent areas matters more than equal depth in all three.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills at various levels of the business and technology organizations: adapting how you make a case depending on the audience, building alignment across cross-functional teams, and saying no to a request and explaining why.
A track record of mentoring peers, setting technical standards, or being the expert others escalate to on hard problems.
- Demonstrated ability to solve ambiguous, high-stakes process problems without an existing playbook, operating with a high degree of autonomy while knowing when to pull others in on high-impact decisions.
Examples include international expansion and multi-entity or multi-currency complexity, or new product offerings where pricing, billing model, and revenue recognition treatment have to be designed together.
- Deep understanding of leading and emerging trends in SaaS finance applications and architecture, including where automation and AI are truly driving innovation.
- Direct experience implementing best practices around change management, regression and UAT planning, segregation of duties, and regulatory requirements, while increasing efficiencies.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
We are investing in our owned social channels to grow share of voice and tell a clearer, more connected company story across LinkedIn, X, Instagram and YouTube.
We need someone to take direct ownership of X and run it day to day, while also maintaining consistent social performance data analysis across all of our owned channels.
This is a hands-on social strategy role for someone who knows how to build an interesting, credible and active presence on X.
You will also work with the Social Manager to turn channel and audience data into clear recommendations about what Harvey should create, publish, test, stop and scale.
The goal is a steady feedback loop between how our audience behaves, what our content strategy is and how our creative gets made.
section_responsibilities:
OWN X STRATEGY AND EXECUTION
- Own Harvey's X strategy, programming and daily execution.
- Develop a distinctive voice and a clear role for Harvey on the platform.
- Create posts built for X, not LinkedIn content with the formatting changed.
- Find proactive, reactive and real-time opportunities for Harvey to join relevant conversations.
- Support product launches, research, events, partnerships, customer stories and company announcements on X.
- Build recurring formats and programming that give people a reason to come back.
- Write and edit copy that is clear, sharp and right for the platform.
- Monitor replies, mentions and relevant conversations.
- Work with the Social Content and Community Manager on engagement and response coverage.
- Support founder, executive and employee amplification where it makes sense.
- Use sound judgment in moments that carry brand, reputational or customer sensitivity.
- Track changes to X and adjust our approach as the platform evolves.
MANAGING CROSS-CHANNEL INSIGHTS AND OPTIMIZATION
- Work with Social Manager and Social Content and Community Manager to pull weekly and monthly performance analysis across X, LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube.
- Collaborate with the social team to go beyond surface metrics and explain what actually drove performance.
- Identify patterns across format, topic, audience, timing, creative approach and distribution.
- Help turn findings into specific programming and creative recommendations.
- Work with third party analytics tools to track follower growth, reach, engagement, clicks, sentiment and other channel-specific signals.
- Analyze performance during major launches, events and campaigns utilizing third party analytics and channel analytics.
- Work with Content Operations on data accuracy, UTMs, reporting processes and dashboards.
- Bring audience and performance insight into quarterly strategy and planning.
PUT SOCIAL LISTENING AND COMPETITIVE INTELLIGENCE TO WORK
- Review owned and third party findings on legal AI conversations, share of voice and competitor activity.
- Separate meaningful signals from routine noise.
- Connect listening and competitive insights with channel performance data to build a fuller picture of what is working.
- Translate audience questions, competitor moves and emerging conversations into programming and creative recommendations.
- Write concise readouts for Social, Marketing and company leadership.
- Flag opportunities and risks early enough for the team to act on them.
SUPPORT THE BROADER SOCIAL TEAM
- Partner closely with the Social Manager on channel strategy, campaign planning and editorial priorities.
- Help translate company priorities into programming for each platform.
- Bring performance insight into the creative briefing process.
- Support social coverage during major events and launches.
- Collaborate with Content, Communications, Product Marketing, Customer Engagement and Harvey Creative Studio.
- Help build repeatable processes without adding unnecessary approval layers.
- Do the work yourself while also improving how the team makes decisions.
WHAT YOU HAVE
- 5+ years of experience in social strategy, social media, audience development, digital publishing or a related field.
- Deep knowledge of X and a track record of growing or reshaping a meaningful brand presence there.
- Strong editorial judgment and the ability to write sharp copy that fits the platform.
- Experience running an active social channel in a fast-moving environment.
- Strong analytical skills and comfort working with social performance data.
- The ability to explain why content performed the way it did, not just report the numbers.
- Experience using social listening, competitive analysis and share-of-voice data to inform strategy.
- A habit of turning data into specific creative and programming recommendations.
- Experience designing social tests and evaluating the results honestly.
- Familiarity with social publishing, analytics and listening platforms.
- Good instincts for real-time content, reputational risk and sensitive moments.
- Experience presenting insights to senior marketing or company leaders.
- Excellent communication skills and a collaborative way of working.
- Comfort making good calls with incomplete information and shifting priorities.
- Genuine interest in legal technology, AI and how professional work is changing.
You do not need to be a data scientist.
We care about analytical fluency, curiosity and the ability to tell a clear story with data, combined with strong social instincts.
Helpful but not required: Experience in B2B technology, media, professional services, legal or another complex industry.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey is transforming how legal and professional services work gets done.
As AI moves from answering questions to carrying out complex workflows, the engineering challenge expands: every interaction depends on systems that can handle sensitive data, stream results, coordinate work, and stay fast and reliable under growing demand.
Backend Platform builds the shared foundations that make this possible.
We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team shaping how backend software is built at Harvey.
Your team owns the frameworks, libraries, and core abstractions that product engineers use every day-from database access and caching to request handling, observability, and safe context propagation.
A better abstraction here can accelerate every product team.
A stronger default can prevent an entire class of production failures.
The impact of your decisions compounds across the engineering organization.
The next chapter is especially compelling.
As both engineers and coding agents contribute more software, we need a platform that makes the right patterns easy to use and the wrong ones difficult to introduce.
You'll help define that foundation: clear architectural boundaries, reusable building blocks, and automated safeguards that let teams ship with confidence.
You'll tackle deep systems problems while building an engineering experience people love.
This is a technical leadership role with room to shape both the platform and the team.
You'll hire and develop exceptional engineers, set the technical direction, and stay close to architecture and code.
If you enjoy turning hard, recurring problems into simple tools that make everyone around you more effective, this is an opportunity to do it at the center of Harvey's growth.
section_responsibilities:
- Lead and grow the Backend Platform team.
Hire, coach, and retain exceptional engineers, giving them clear ownership, meaningful technical challenges, and room to grow.

Partner with product engineering teams to understand their hardest problems, identify the investments with the broadest impact, and deliver improvements they can feel in their daily work.

Make read replicas usable and move high-volume data off the primary.

Reduce latency, improve observability, and make production issues easier to diagnose.

- Clear communication and the ability to lead across team boundaries, align people on technical tradeoffs, and drive changes from design through rollout.
- Serious, hands-on use of AI coding agents, and opinions on what makes a codebase safe for them to work in.

job_title: Senior Manager, Product Design, Admin and Enterprise Platform
section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
We're looking for a Senior Manager, Product Design to lead the Admin & Enterprise Platform
Admin is how firm leaders and innovation teams set up and run Harvey inside their organizations: workflow configuration, permissions and governance, and visibility into how the product is being used.
These are the people who decide whether Harvey stays at an account, and Admin is where they see what they're getting from it.
Enterprise Platform owns the context and knowledge layer every Harvey product builds from: document management integrations, Vault, connectors, and the research hub.
A general model can reason about law, but it can't reach a firm's precedent or matter files that a lawyer would actually cite.
It also can't be trusted with them by default, so this team owns how that context is secured and permissioned.
What the rest of the product can do is empowered by what this context layer can reach, and design decides whether a lawyer can tell what Harvey found and what it missed.
You'll report to the VP Design as a foundational member of the Design leadership team, with portfolio-wide impact on how our product, team, and culture scale.
You'll set the operating bar for how we work, and lay foundations for the product that hold for years.

Own Admin and Enterprise as a product
- Drive strategy and execution for the Admin & Enterprise platforms in close partnership with Product and Engineering, rooted in how champions actually run Harvey inside their firms.
- Work directly with customers, research, and usage data to find where champions lose time or lose confidence, and design the workflow configuration, knowledge management, and visibility experiences that fix it.
- Tie your roadmap to customer outcomes: faster rollout, wider adoption, and evidence of ROI our champions can take to their own leadership.
Build and lead the team
- Build, grow, and develop a team of high-craft ICs across systems, product, and prototyping from a small starting footprint.
- Own org design, resourcing, and prioritization across four surfaces with very different rhythms, including the conference deadlines that don't move.
- Give strategic, systems-level feedback on end-to-end flows, not just screens.
Lead across the org
- Partner with design, product, and engineering leaders to evolve how Harvey builds, and represent Platform in high-stakes conversations with executives and customers.

- Be a foundational member of the Design leadership team and help set the operating model the rest of the org runs on.

- Empathy for users, teammates, and the realities of high-stakes professional work.

When we amplify a moment, it should land everywhere our people and audiences are.

That means managing DMs, comments, and mentions; moderating and growing our community spaces; sending questions and opportunities to the right teams; and starting conversations that draw people toward Harvey.

section_responsibilities:

- Write copy for employee and advocacy channels to power company amplification.

- Ability to move quickly on real-time moments while keeping quality and brand safety high.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey's content roadmap keeps getting bigger.
It now covers editorial, research and reports, video, social, educational programming, events, executive content and recurring franchises.
Our biggest ideas no longer fit in a single asset.
Each one needs a connected program with a clear idea at the center and someone who can carry it from the first conversation to launch.
That is the job.
As Director, Integrated Content Programs, you will be the showrunner for Harvey's highest-priority, multi-format content programs.
You will take a strategic priority or a rough idea, work out what it should become, and come back with a strong recommendation.
Then you will lead it through development, production, distribution and delivery.
This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role.
You will lead through influence.
That means you pull together writers, editors, social strategists, designers, producers, agencies, subject-matter experts and executives around one shared idea.
As the program grows, this role may build a team.
This is not a project management role.
We are looking for someone with the editorial judgment and creative instincts to shape the work itself, and the operational discipline to get it made well.
THE KIND OF WORK YOU'LL LEAD
A typical program might start as a single sentence from leadership, an insight from our research, or a moment on the company calendar.
Your job is to find the idea inside it and build it into something bigger.
That could be a flagship piece supported by editorial, video, social and event content, with each part designed to strengthen the others.
The programs you lead will generally fall into a few categories:
- Flagship research and reports, with the campaigns built around them
- Educational programs for the legal and professional community
- Content captured at and around live events
- Recurring video, audio and editorial franchises
- Executive, customer and talent-led storytelling
- Connected content systems for major product and company moments

Lead the program from concept to launch

- Set up workstreams, owners, decision points and creative review milestones
- Choose the right internal capabilities, external partners and production approach for each project
- Anticipate risks and solve problems before they compromise the brief, the timeline or the final work
Direct the creative work

- Stay hands-on, especially during concept development, briefing, story development and creative review
Bring the right people together
- Direct and coordinate writers, editors, social strategists, designers, producers, agencies, subject-matter experts and executive stakeholders
- Work with Content Operations on schedules, dependencies, workflow and delivery
- Work with Social on platform strategy, distribution and audience development
- Work with Harvey Creative Studio on visual development, brand expression, design, motion and production
- Work with Product Marketing, Communications, Events, Research and company leaders to gather inputs and keep everyone aligned
Build what lasts
- Use performance and audience insights to improve future programming
- Turn successful programs into repeatable formats, franchises and playbooks

- A portfolio of distinctive programs that span more than one format
- Strong storytelling, editorial judgment and creative instincts

- Strong brief writing and presentation skills
- A track record of leading complex, visible initiatives with many stakeholders
- The ability to work well with executives and subject-matter experts, and to get the best out of them on camera and on the page
- Experience directing agencies, production companies, writers, designers and filmmakers
- A solid understanding of video, social, editorial, research, education and event content
- Enough production and budget fluency to make creative recommendations that can actually be made
- The ability to hold a premium brand standard while moving quickly and staying relevant on each platform
- Sound decision-making, prioritization and communication
- Comfort in a fast-moving company where priorities and inputs change
- A low-ego, collaborative working style
- Real curiosity about legal technology, AI and how professional work is changing
Experience in the legal industry is helpful but not required.
We care more about your judgment, your craft and your ability to learn a complex subject quickly.

section_intro:
WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Harvey is transforming how legal and professional services work gets done.
As AI moves from answering questions to carrying out complex workflows, the engineering challenge expands: every interaction depends on systems that can handle sensitive data, stream results, coordinate work, and stay fast and reliable under growing demand.
Backend Platform builds the shared foundations that make this possible.
We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the team shaping how backend software is built at Harvey.
Your team owns the frameworks, libraries, and core abstractions that product engineers use every day-from database access and caching to request handling, observability, and safe context propagation.
A better abstraction here can accelerate every product team.
A stronger default can prevent an entire class of production failures.
The impact of your decisions compounds across the engineering organization.
The next chapter is especially compelling.
As both engineers and coding agents contribute more software, we need a platform that makes the right patterns easy to use and the wrong ones difficult to introduce.
You'll help define that foundation: clear architectural boundaries, reusable building blocks, and automated safeguards that let teams ship with confidence.
You'll tackle deep systems problems while building an engineering experience people love.
This is a technical leadership role with room to shape both the platform and the team.
You'll hire and develop exceptional engineers, set the technical direction, and stay close to architecture and code.
If you enjoy turning hard, recurring problems into simple tools that make everyone around you more effective, this is an opportunity to do it at the center of Harvey's growth.
section_responsibilities:
- Lead and grow the Backend Platform team.
Hire, coach, and retain exceptional engineers, giving them clear ownership, meaningful technical challenges, and room to grow.
- Define the platform's technical vision and roadmap.
Partner with product engineering teams to understand their hardest problems, identify the investments with the broadest impact, and deliver improvements they can feel in their daily work.
- Build the next generation of Harvey's backend foundations.
Guide the design of shared frameworks for database access, session management, caching, request handling, and streaming-with clear interfaces and strong defaults.
- Help Harvey scale through better architecture.
Work with Infrastructure to evolve how applications use databases, replicas, and new storage systems, making those capabilities accessible without requiring every product team to solve the same problems.
- Scale the data layer.
Build a data access layer so an entity can move to a new store (KV, NoSQL) without product changes.
Make read replicas usable and move high-volume data off the primary.
- Make failure boring.
Load test until "what happens at 3x?" has a real answer.
Add circuit breakers, a standard outbound client with timeouts, retries and idempotency, and noisy-neighbor isolation, so one workspace or one slow vendor can't take down the platform.
- Make security and reliability properties of the platform.
Partner with Security and product teams on safe handling of customer data, workspace isolation, and safeguards that prevent recurring failure patterns before code reaches production.
- Shape a codebase that humans and AI can build in confidently.
Establish modular boundaries, enforceable contracts, and automated checks that make changes easier to reason about, review, and ship.
- Turn platform improvements into customer impact.
Reduce latency, improve observability, and make production issues easier to diagnose.
Measure success through adoption, developer productivity, and the performance and reliability of the products built on your work.

Lead architecture discussions, review critical code, prototype when useful, and help engineers navigate difficult tradeoffs.
Partner closely with Infrastructure, Developer Platform, Model Infrastructure, Security, and product engineering leaders to carry changes through to adoption.

- Experience building shared libraries, frameworks, or internal platforms adopted by multiple engineering teams.
You know how to balance a useful abstraction with the flexibility its users need.
- The technical depth to engage directly in design and code reviews, investigate difficult systems problems, and guide migrations across a large, evolving codebase.

- A track record of hiring, coaching, and developing engineers, setting clear expectations, and creating a culture of ownership and thoughtful execution.
- Strong product instincts for developer tools.
You listen closely to engineers, understand where they lose time, and turn that feedback into simpler, more effective ways to build.
- Experience embedding reliability, observability, and security into shared systems, with measurable improvements in production.
- Clear communication and the ability to lead across team boundaries, align people on technical tradeoffs, and drive changes from design through rollout.
- Serious, hands-on use of AI coding agents, and opinions on what makes a codebase safe for them to work in.

WHY HARVEY
ROLE OVERVIEW
Customer Experience runs on data - but right now, that data lives in too many places, speaks too many languages, and reaches the wrong people too late.

You'll build and maintain the dashboards, reports, and feedback loops that tell us whether we're hitting our north stars - cSAT, TTR, QA scores, escalation rates - and surface the signal underneath the numbers so we can act on it.
You'll sit within the Support Operations team, reporting to the Support Operations Manager, and work closely with Customer Experience leadership and Harvey's central data team to ensure the org is equipped with the right instrumentation as we scale.
This is a solo role.
You won't have a team beneath you.

- Track ticket deflection, AI/chatbot performance, and self-service effectiveness

You push back when framing is wrong
- Clarity: your outputs are direct, jargon-free, and actionable.

ROLE OVERVIEW
Customer Experience runs on data - but right now, that data lives in too many places, speaks too many languages, and reaches the wrong people too late.
This role exists to fix that.

You'll build and maintain the dashboards, reports, and feedback loops that tell us whether we're hitting our north stars - cSAT, TTR, QA scores, escalation rates - and surface the signal underneath the numbers so we can act on it.
You'll sit within the Support Operations team, reporting to the Support Operations Manager, and work closely with Customer Experience leadership and Harvey's central data team to ensure the org is equipped with the right instrumentation as we scale.
This is a solo role.
You won't have a team beneath you.
You will need to be fluent enough in support analytics to hold the function independently, confident enough to push back on how metrics are framed, and fast enough to operate at Harvey's pace.
section_responsibilities:
- Own recurring reporting for Customer Experience - weekly, monthly, and QBR-ready - tailored to ops, leadership, and cross-functional audiences
- Translate support data into clear narratives: what's happening, why, and what to do about it
- Track and maintain north star metrics: cSAT, TTR by tier, QA scores, bug escalation rate to EPD, and First Response Time
- Build and maintain self-serve dashboards that give the ops team and leadership real-time visibility into support performance
- Partner with Support Systems to ensure Zendesk is instrumented to capture the data we need
- Work with Harvey's central data team to connect support data to broader product and customer data sources
- Identify and close data collection gaps - if we can't measure it, help define how we should
- Design feedback loops that connect support signals to Product, Engineering, and Customer Success
- Quantify the operational cost of product bugs, feature gaps, and onboarding failures
- Contribute to QA analytics as the QA program matures
- Track ticket deflection, AI/chatbot performance, and self-service effectiveness
- Measure the impact of AI-driven support - containment rate, escalation rate from AI interactions, resolution quality - and surface findings that drive how we tune and invest in those tools
- Support ad hoc analytical requests from the Support Operations Manager, Customer Experience leadership, and senior stakeholders

- 3-5 years of experience in analytics, with at least 2 years directly in support operations, customer success operations, or a closely adjacent function
- Fluency in support platform data - you know how Zendesk (or equivalent) is structured, what data it produces, and what it doesn't
- SQL proficiency - you can write complex queries against large datasets without hand-holding (CTEs, window functions, joins across schemas)
- Dashboard experience - you've built and maintained operational dashboards in Looker, Tableau, Sigma, Omni, or equivalent
- Reporting for multiple audiences - you know the difference between what a frontline manager needs and what a CFO needs, and you build accordingly
- Strong data storytelling - you don't just present numbers, you write the narrative
- Comfort operating solo - you don't need a team around you to deliver, and you don't need a ticket to tell you what to look at
Strong Plus
- Experience with Python for data manipulation or automation
- Familiarity with dbt or similar data transformation tooling
- Experience building or contributing to QA analytics programs
- Background supporting enterprise SaaS or AI-native products
- Experience working with Zendesk APIs or extracting data beyond standard reporting

- AI-native: you use AI tooling actively in your analytical workflows - not as a novelty, but as a force multiplier
- Pace: you move in hours and days, not weeks.
You surface findings before anyone has to ask
- Judgment: you know which metrics matter and which are vanity.
You push back when framing is wrong
- Clarity: your outputs are direct, jargon-free, and actionable.
You write for the reader, not yourself
- Ownership: you treat Customer Experience analytics as your problem to solve, not a ticket queue to process
